holisticNarrative.summary:
The primary evidence is a concise compliance-focused PDF that clearly communicates packaging and standards at a high level: exports can run for one patient or a full population, output is delivered as zip bundle(s), and the bundle includes clinical C-CDA files, adhoc patient-note CSV files, and scanned-record CDA/XML files. This is enough to establish that a real, usable export function exists and that it spans both clinical and financial-adjacent data categories (via billing-record and claim-data references).

The migration concern is model fidelity rather than total absence. The documentation exposes almost no operational data model structure: no machine-readable schema, no sample bundle, no relationship map, and no detailed claim-data dictionary even though claim files are named in the file convention. That combination increases projection-loss and reconstruction risk, especially for payment-impacting billing semantics.

Applying the EHI scope boundary in this review narrows the deficiency focus to patient-specific clinical and billing decision data. Operational artifacts such as audit/access logs are not treated as missing EHI. Within that scoped lens, the export appears directionally useful but materially under-documented for robust, low-assumption migration workflows.
standoutObservations: Strongest direct artifact: explicit single-patient and full-collection zip export description with mixed-format contents.
Most consequential gap: claim/billing data is acknowledged but structurally undocumented.
Documentation depth is uneven: one concrete table for patNotes, but no equivalent detail for major clinical/financial payloads.

notableFacts: The export guide states outputs may contain one patient or a full patient collection and are delivered as zip file(s).
Clinical payload is declared as HL7 C-CDA R2.1 with XML + HTML pairing.
Adhoc patient/telephone notes are exported as a `patNotes` CSV with 7 documented columns and per-column meaning text.
Scanned/uploaded records are exported as `Echart` XML/CDA payloads containing Base64-encoded document content.
The document states self-service export has no associated fee, while vendor-performed export may incur time-and-effort-based fees.
Claim Data appears in filename TYPE examples, but the document does not provide a claim-data schema or field dictionary.
